ca_echo_cove.blurb: Echo Cove is a compact, busy pocket of the Echo Rock area in the central part of Joshua Tree National Park, near Hidden Valley. Traditional climbing leads, with a big helping of boulder problems, some top-rope routes and a handful of bolted lines. Routes run from easy moderates to 5.12, though most sit around 5.10 and 5.11, and the boulder problems stretch from very easy to V7. Bolted face climbs share the cove with cracks, and many routes can be led or top-roped. The surrounding formations are granite. Bases are flat, the approach is easy and the crowds can be heavy. The South Face, East Side and North Side hold most of the routes, with several small boulders scattered nearby.

ca_whitney_portal.blurb: Whitney Portal sits high in the Eastern Sierra above Lone Pine, at roughly 8,400 feet, up the road that runs west past the Alabama Hills. Traditional climbing dominates, with some sport routes, a few top-rope and aid lines, and a small set of boulder problems. Most routes fall around 5.10, with a fair number from 5.7 through 5.12 and only a couple harder. Short cragging mixes with a few long multi-pitch lines on bigger walls. One roadside cliff near the east end is clean granite with splitter cracks and black knobs. Roadwork Wall, The Beach, Candlelight Buttress and Whitney Portal Buttress are among the larger crags.

ma_townsend_ma_bouldering.blurb: Townsend, MA Bouldering is a scatter of small boulder spots around the town of Townsend in eastern Massachusetts. Nearly everything is bouldering, with a broad spread from V0 up to V7 and most problems between V0 and V3. The rock is mainly granite in scattered boulders and exposed ledges, with some sandy, schist-like stone too, and quality varies from spot to spot. Willard Brook State Forest, on the Townsend and Ashby border, tucks boulders and faces into mountain laurel, with some choss beside good granite. At State Line Boulders the rock is gritty and many problems start under overhangs. Barker Hill and Fessenden Crag round out the larger spots.

ca_sugarloaf_area.blurb: Sugarloaf Area lies along Highway 50 between Placerville and Lake Tahoe, near Kyburz, in Eldorado National Forest at around 4,000 feet. The centrepiece is a granite spire of roughly 350 feet, ringed by smaller crags and boulders. Trad leads, sport follows close behind, and there are a few boulder problems and top-rope routes. Grades spread from easy to hard, though most sit between 5.9 and 5.12. The main spire faces mostly south-southwest, and its lower elevation makes it an excellent winter crag. Many separate formations sit along the trail, including Midway Rock, Sugarbun, West Buttress and Split Rock.

mo_em_silver_mines.blurb: Silver Mines is a former mining site in Missouri's Mark Twain National Forest, set along the St. Francis River in wooded country with bluffs on both banks. The rock here is Precambrian granite and felsite. Bouldering makes up most of the climbing, from very easy problems up to V7 with most in the V0 to V3 range, alongside a good number of trad routes and a few top-ropes running from 5.6 into the 5.12s. The climbing splits into an East Side (River Left) and a West Side (River Right), each broken into many small boulders and short walls.

_skipped.co_black_wave_boulder_area: Sub-area of Nine Mile Bouldering; the only fetchable pages (Nine Mile Bouldering, Nine Mile Hill) are about its parent, and none describes Black Wave itself.
